chapter: Mamie Smith and the New York dance bands
title: Dance schools and society bands: Happy Roark and Lucky Roberts
summary: After Mamie he worked dance schools and large society dance bands, which paid well.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, so where did you quit Mamie?
In New York.
Oh, and then what?
Back to (unintelligible) -- I got out from the road

of the band, and we stayed around New York, went to the dancing school, then working with different ones. Then I joined the -- at that time they had -- playing these big colored dances, was a fellow named Happy Roark had a big band and played for all the big society clubs. And John C. Smith, trumpet player, he played at all the society clubs around New York, and they had those 14, 15, 16 piece band then.
Well, they would be playing sort of more or less like dance music.
That's right.
They weren't playing sort of (unintelligible).
(Laughter)
Dance music, that's right.
So it was a kind of a society --
Kind of a society, that's what it was, right. That's right.
But that was where you could get work.
Good work, good pay.
Yeah.
More than that, we could get those -- we used to call it gig. You did it three times a week, you had enough. The salaries, you make over $100.00 and some.
Yeah. Well, there was -- that's like -- what was that other guy? Oh, Lucky Roberts.
Lucky Roberts, worked with Lucky Roberts too.
I mean that was what he did.
That's right.
